show.name: A Child's Christmas in Wales - Lighthouse Theatre
show.description:
Lighthouse Theatre

presents

A Child's Christmas

by

Dylan Thomas and Richard Burton

A Child's Christmas in Wales by Dylan Thomas

‘Snow grew overnight on the roofs of the houses’

Dylan Thomas and Richard Burton are icons of twentieth century Wales. They have produced stories about Christmases in Wales that rival Charles Dickens’ short stories about Christmas in nineteenth century England. In some ways  Thomas and Burton can be accused of inventing Christmas in exactly the same way Dickens is responsible for creating the Christmas that we enjoy so wholeheartedly.

For all of that, however, Burton and Thomas were actors whose love of words shines through these two short but heart-warming stories.

Described by the South Wales Evening Post as ‘a joy’, this ‘Welsh Icons Xmas show’ performed by two actors has proved hugely popular - Join Lighthouse as they conjure up Christmas in the air....

" Mae'r Nadolig wedi ddechre'n bendant nawr."

"Two mesmerising performances. A wonderful afternoon of festive theatre."

‘There were very few white Christmases in my part of Wales’….

A Christmas Story by Richard Burton

show.name: Bara Caws: Bugail Geifr
show.description:
Bara Caws has hit the Big 50! Just think what this remarkable company has given us as a nation over the years. The serious, the challenging, the entertainment and fun. Hours and hours of showing ourselves to ourselves, and shocking us into self-recognition from time to time.

How to respond to this?That’s up to you. But let’s try.

My own response is Y Bugail Geifr. I’ve called it a verse-drama in the form of a monologue. Its only purpose is to pay blunt, unflinching tribute to the Company from someone who has had the privilege of writing several shows for them. To say Thank You — that’s all. But in a way that asks the question: What is the beating heart of theatre? It is also a song of praise to theatre itself.

And to get Dyfan Roberts into action! One of the company’s founding fathers. It’s for the voice of a particular actor that I write these days.It is Dyfan’s voice that shines through this piece. But there are other voices too — voices that have contributed to the life of Bara Caws.

Y Bugail Geifr is full of spirits. One actor… but a multitude of individuals.

Aled Jones Williams.

This is the last theatre play of the giant of a playwright Aled Jones Williams who has been part of the theatrical landscape here in Wales for over three decades.

His last treasure? A gift to Theatr Bara Caws as we begin our 50th anniversary celebrations.

A play specially written for Dyfan Roberts, one of the founders of the Company back in 1976/77.

Ffion Dafis

Cast : Dyfan Roberts

Director : Betsan Llwyd

show.description:
GIANT, the 5-star critically acclaimed play starring John Lithgow (Killers of the Flower Moon, The Crown) as Roald Dahl, comes to the big screen. Winner of 3 Olivier Awards® including Best Play and a Tony Award® for Best Actor in a Play (John Lithgow), the production was filmed live in London’s West End ahead of its sold-out Broadway run. The stellar cast includes Aya Cash (The Boys, The Franchise, You’re the Worst), Elliot Levey (Cold War, Patriots, Good) and Rachael Stirling (The Divine Mrs S).

A world-famous children’s author under threat. A battle of wills in the wake of scandal. And one chance to make amends...It’s the summer of 1983, The Witches is about to hit the shelves and Roald Dahl is making last-minute edits. But the outcry at his recent, explicitly antisemitic article won’t die down. Across a single afternoon at his family home, and rocked by an unexpectedly explosive confrontation, Dahl is forced to choose: make a public apology or risk his name and reputation. Inspired by real events, GIANT explores with dark humour the difference between considered opinion and dangerous rhetoric offering a complicated portrait of a fiendishly charismatic icon.

show.name: Lighthouse Theatre: The Chimes: Dickens on Air
show.description:
Lighthouse Theatre and Pontardawe Arts Centre

present

WAFR: Playhouse of the Air in

The Chimes: Dickens on Air

'A Festive Story to Ring the Old Year Out and the New Year In.'

It is Christmas 1950 in New York and the actors of WAFR: Playhouse of the Air gather for their annual festive broadcast...There is a new government, a new hope, a new world, so what better than a new play? And there is no better story-teller than Charles Dickens - and there is no better man to keep Christmas than he!

Trotty Veck is a ticket-porter – a man who fetches and carries packages, letters and deliveries for a small sixpence here and there. He doesn’t have much but he is happy, gentle and lives a simple, obedient life.

That life is given its order by the sound of the bells of his local church – breakfast, lunch, dinner all from the sound of the bells. He sometimes even hears them speaking to him…

In the run-up to the festive season Trotty falls asleep after a long day’s carrying and delivering. Woken by the church bells, The Chimes, and then summoned up the tower by their mysterious power, he has just one chance to change this world… but will he listen to the bells?

The Chimes is a Victorian It’s a Wonderful Life filled with all of the master story-teller’s colourful characters and heart-rending poignancy.

Fresh their hugely popular adaptations of A Christmas Carol and Casablanca, Lighthouse Theatre brings their signature live radio play style to this classic by the most theatrical of authors. There will be jingles, carols, music and – of course – bells!…this show is sure to be fast and funny, inventive and entertaining; but most of all a Christmas treat to reinforce the message of this festive time of the year…

Recommended for ages 10 and above.

Presented in conjunction with Arts Council Wales

show.description:
Welsh language production


AN EVENING WITH HYWEL AND BETI

Ad/lib Cymru presents two icons of Welsh broadcasting: Hywel Gwynfryn and Beti George. Both are now in their eighties, but they must be eating something very special for breakfast because they each look much younger than their years! It is also wonderful that both continue to work regularly with S4C and, of course, BBC Radio Cymru. Without doubt, the world of Welsh broadcasting would be much poorer without them.

Their voices and faces have been part of Welsh homes since the 1960s. Just imagine the stories they have to tell.

In An Evening with Hywel and Beti, audiences will have the opportunity to hear those stories as Hywel and Beti come together on stage. During the first half of the show, Hywel will interview Beti, and in the second half, Beti will turn the tables and interview Hywel.

We will hear about Beti’s early years in Coed-y-Bryn, Ceredigion, as well as Hywel’s childhood on Anglesey, many years before they both made their way to Cardiff – Hywel to study at the Welsh College of Music and Drama in the 1960s, and Beti following a period with the BBC in Swansea.

A truly unique and memorable evening not to be missed.

show.name: Noson Yng Nghwmni Sue Roderick
show.description:
An Evening with Sue Roderick

This special event looks back on the life and career of the actress from Porthmadog. Sue began singing from a young age and performed with Treflyn Jones in the duo “Treflyn a Siwsan.” At just ten years old, she appeared on Disc a Dawn (BBC Wales). Four years later, she auditioned for Cwmni Theatr Cymru. Although she was considered too young to start working with the company, she was offered singing lessons by Betty Roberts, wife of the company’s director, Wilbert Roberts. After leaving school, Sue returned to work with Cwmni Theatr Cymru.

In 1987, she appeared in Codi Pais (HTV), an entertainment programme featuring sketches and songs. The show broke new ground for women in comedy, showcasing the talents of Sue alongside Siw Hughes, Gillian Elisa and Eirlys Parri.

Sue was one of the leading actors in the acclaimed film Hedd Wyn, attending the Academy Awards and meeting a number of Hollywood’s biggest stars. She also appeared in Twin Town, playing Lucy Cartwright. During the 1990s, she starred in television dramas including Minafod, Y Palmant Aur and Yr Heliwr, before joining the cast of Pobol y Cwm as Cassie Morris, co-owner of the Deri Arms with her husband, Teg. After leaving the soap in 2003, she returned to Pobol y Cwm at the end of 2018 in a storyline involving the scattering of Mrs Mac’s ashes.

The Deri was not the only fictional pub where Sue worked. She also played Megan Morgan, a barmaid in the Rovers Return in Coronation Street, alongside Alec Gilroy and Bet Lynch.

During the first half of the evening, Ieuan Rhys will interview Sue about her life and career, while the second half will give audience members the opportunity to ask their own questions.

And who knows—perhaps Sue will even treat us to a song or two before the night is over!

An enjoyable evening in the company of one of Wales’s busiest and most beloved actors. A night to remember.

Hay Fever by Noël Coward

directed by Emily Burns

Emmy and Tony winner Christine Baranski makes her West End debut alongside Academy Award-nominated stage and screen legend Richard E. Grant in Noël Coward’s irresistible comedy.

Judith Bliss retired from her life-on-stage and she misses the applause. Idling away at their country home, the rest of the family are too self-involved to be a good audience. So, Judith invites a young fan as her guest for the weekend. But unbeknownst to her, each of the Blisses has a guest of their own arriving at the very same time.

Filmed live from the West End, Emily Burns directs this stinging new production.

show.name: NT Live: The Misanthrope
show.description:
The Misanthrope by Martin Crimp

after Molière

directed by Indhu Rubasingham

Award-winner Sandra Oh (Killing Eve) plays the title role in this razor-sharp reimagining of Molière’s classic dark comedy.

Telling the truth isn’t always that simple. Alice, a brilliant novelist, despises the carefully constructed lies of modern society. But the more she challenges those around her, the fiercer the backlash becomes. Soon, she must confront the price of speaking her truth in a world that would rather silence her.

Filmed live on stage at the National Theatre, Indhu Rubasingham directs Martin Crimp’s (Cyrano de Bergerac) highly anticipated play.

show.name: The FM Songbook The Ultimate Fleetwood Mac Tribute
show.description:
The FM Songbook - The Ultimate Tribute to Fleetwood Mac

(formerly The Fleetwood Mac Songbook)

“Witnessing The FM Songbook live in action, is like capturing a little sprinkling of stardust”.

Kelly Scanlon, Far Out Magazine

Earning rave reviews wherever they play and ranked in the 'Top 20 Tribute Artists & Bands in the UK’ by Champions UK plc Entertainment Agency, six-piece tribute band 'The FM Songbook' are not to be missed.

The band perform a spell binding tribute performance of the stellar 'songbook' of 'Fleetwood Mac', drawing from over SIX decades of hits from one of the greatest and most loved bands in music history. Their set of course includes soft rock anthems from the 'Rumours' album and the shimmering 80s brilliance of 'Tango in the Night' and there’s a very respectful top hat nod to the raw blues of the 'Peter Green' era. There may even be a Stevie solo in there somewhere!

Expect all the classics; Dreams, Go Your Own Way, Don’t Stop, Silver Springs, Everywhere, Songbird, The Chain, Tusk plus so many more and get ready to sing, dance and relive the magic of Fleetwood Mac.

Attention to detail ensures the unmistakable 'Mac' sound is recreated faithfully - the exceptional three-part harmonies are a standout – this show is a masterclass in musical magic.

You will be assured of a night to remember in the company of these fine musicians - an unforgettable evening suitable for all ages.

show.name: The Silent Volunteer
show.description:
In a moving tribute to all those affected by the Aberfan disaster, The Silent Volunteer asks the question, “Have we learnt from our mistakes?” Lovingly performed by a cast affected by what happened that Friday morning 60 years ago, the play explores the enormous role volunteers played in the aftermath, and how the events of 1966 have continued to shape mining communities ever since.

The Silent Volunteer is a play about voices that have not yet found the words to speak — but who want the world to know the Aberfan disaster was not “an act of God”, and that future disasters in former mining areas can and must be prevented.

Avant Cymru presents The Silent Volunteer, a play by Sue Bevan, alongside an exhibition and Q&A in partnership with Coalfield Regeneration.

To mark the 60th anniversary of the Aberfan Disaster, the descendants of the volunteers are opening up a conversation about how this history continues to shape mining communities today — and why remembering, listening and learning still matters.

show.name: Tommy Cooper
show.description:
A brand new production from the guys that brought you Steptoe & Son!


Tommy Cooper, one of the greatest ever comedians, is back! Expertly performed by Phil Hoyles - the UK's number one impersonator - he brings you all of the 'tom'-foolery, jokes, songs, laughs, magic, failed magic, and energy, that the original funnyman presented all those years ago!
Renowned theatre magazine The Stage describes Phil's portrayal as "a carbon copy in look, voice and humour" and "as near to the genuine article as you can get"!


He's got the height, the laugh and the Fez - all we need is you! Come along and join us for a trip down memory lane, a jolly good laugh and an evening of belly-aching nostalgia.


This show is being produced by Cattle Productions Ltd. who have a distinguished reputation in the revival and recreation of classic comedy, ensuring that these true icons are never forgotten.


We are also supporting local charity RNLI Abersoch Lifeboat Station from the proceeds.

show.name: Twin Town + Q&A Kevin Allen (18)
show.description:
This... is Welsh film. Discover new stories, Re-watch the classics. Celebrate 130 years of cinema in Wales

Join us for a special screening of the iconic dark comedy Twin Town with our special guest director of the film Kevin Allen. Julian and Jeremy, two brothers known as the "Lewis Twins", prefer to spend their time on drugs and joyriding. When their father, Fatty Lewis, breaks his leg working for local bigwig Bryn Cartwright, they show up demanding compensation. Underestimating the vicious humour of the twins, Bryn brusquely refuses to pay for the uninsured Fatty and unleashes a ferocious feud.

Ticket prices increase by £1.50 on the day of screening apart from Monday morning and Wednesday afternoon screening.

Supported by Film Hub Wales as part of the BFI Film Audience Network (FAN), made possible by the National Lottery.
